title: How do we find 65 squared by cutting a square into four parts?
description: A square of side sixty five is cut as sixty plus five into a big square, a small square and two rectangles. The areas are added, and a second cut, thirty plus thirty five, gives the same area. Keeko doubts that the two squares are enough.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square of side a plus b is a big square, a small square and two equal rectangles. Watch for students who square each part and add, leaving the two rectangles out.

source: Find 65² by splitting 65 as 60 + 5, and check with the split 30 + 35.
video_script.why: The child has met the four parts of a bracket times a bracket. Here the two brackets are the same, so the four parts make a square.
video_script.substitution: Cut the side into two parts, find the areas of the big square, the small square and the two rectangles, add them, and check with a different cut.
video_script.anchor: a square of side sixty five, cut as sixty plus five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko squares each part and adds, getting three thousand six hundred twenty five. The two rectangles are left out, so the area is too small.
video_script.payoff_line: Two squares and two rectangles make the whole square

final_answer.spoken: sixty five squared is four thousand two hundred twenty five

maths_rules: squaring each part and adding gives 3600 + 25 = 3625, which leaves out the two rectangles of 300 each
video_script.design: One idea: a square cut into two squares and two rectangles. Uses the four parts idea from the distributive property. Wrong idea: square each part and add. The cut square stays on the board through the doubt.

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step one, split the side as sixty plus five.
<bookmark mark='big'/>The big square has side sixty, so its area is three thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The small square has side five, so its area is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>Each of the two rectangles is sixty by five, so its area is three hundred.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add the four areas.
Three thousand six hundred, plus three hundred, plus three hundred, plus twenty five.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>The total is four thousand two hundred twenty five.

<bookmark mark='big'/>The square of side thirty has area nine hundred.
The square of side thirty five has area one thousand two hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>Each rectangle is thirty by thirty five, so its area is one thousand fifty.
